buyer.title: Get ready to buy
items: Get pre-approved: know your real budget before you shop (not just pre-qualified)
Define your must-haves, nice-to-haves, and dealbreakers
Research neighborhoods, school districts, and commute times
Review HOA rules, fees, and any rental or fence restrictions for communities you like
Look up property tax rates and typical utility costs for the areas you're considering
Start touring homes and attending open houses
Build your cash-to-close fund: closing costs typically run 2-4% of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs
Connect with a Realtor you trust and sign a buyer representation agreement
buyer.tip: Pro tip: avoid opening new credit, financing furniture, or changing jobs from this point through closing.

buyer.title: Under contract
items: Deliver your earnest money by the deadline in your contract
Schedule a professional home inspection (consider radon, sewer scope, and termite/WDO inspections)
Review inspection results and negotiate repairs or credits within your due diligence period
Secure homeowner's insurance and send proof of coverage to your lender
Stay in close contact with your lender: respond to every request within 24 hours
Confirm the appraisal is ordered (your lender handles this) and your title company is engaged
Order a home warranty if you want one
Begin planning any renovations or improvements for after closing

buyer.title: Plan your move
items: Get moving quotes from at least 3 licensed companies (or reserve a truck); book early for month-end dates
Sort and declutter: don't pay to move what you don't need
Begin packing non-essentials: books, decor, seasonal items
Collect boxes, packing tape, and supplies
Notify your landlord if you're renting (check your lease for notice terms)
Create a moving budget and track expenses

buyer.title: Lock in the details
items: Confirm your moving company or truck reservation in writing
Set up mail forwarding with USPS
Schedule utilities at your new address: electric, gas, water, trash, internet
Update your address with your bank, insurance providers, and employer
Pack room by room: label every box by room and contents
Arrange childcare or pet care for moving day
Transfer or cancel subscriptions and memberships
Review your Closing Disclosure as soon as your lender sends it (you should receive it at least 3 business days before closing). Compare it to your Loan Estimate and ask questions.

buyer.title: Final week
items: Confirm closing date, time, and location with your Realtor and title company
Schedule your final walkthrough of the new home
Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust. Never rely on emailed wire instructions: wire fraud is real.
Confirm exactly how much you need to bring or wire for closing
Pack a "first night" box: toiletries, chargers, sheets, snacks, medications, basic tools
Defrost the freezer and clean out the fridge
Disassemble large furniture as needed
Back up important files and charge all devices

buyer.title: Closing day
items: Bring a valid government-issued photo ID
Bring certified funds (cashier's check) or confirm your wire has been received
Review and sign all closing documents carefully: ask about anything unclear
Receive your keys, garage openers, and any codes or remotes
Confirm utilities are active at your new home
Do a final sweep of your old place before handing it over

buyer.title: Moving day
items: Walk through the new home before unloading and test all major systems: HVAC, plumbing, appliances
Supervise the movers or direct helpers to the right rooms
Check inventory as items come off the truck and note any damage right away
Set up essential rooms first: beds, bathroom, kitchen

buyer.title: Settle in
items: Change all locks and update garage codes, security codes, and smart-home passwords
Locate the main water shutoff, electrical panel, and gas valve
Update your address: DMV, voter registration, subscriptions, IRS
Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; replace batteries
Change HVAC filters and note the service schedule
Register children at their new school
Find local services: doctor, dentist, vet, pharmacy
Keep your closing documents and home inspection report in one safe place
Schedule any planned renovations or improvements
Introduce yourself at the HOA office or to neighbors (if applicable)
Leave a review for your Realtor: it truly means the world!

seller.title: Prepare to sell
items: Interview and choose your Realtor and review the listing agreement, including commission, marketing plan, and term
Request a mortgage payoff estimate from your lender so you know what you owe
Review comparable sales and an estimated net sheet: know what you'll actually walk away with
Schedule a pre-listing home inspection to catch surprises before buyers do
Identify repairs and improvements worth making (ask me which ones pay off in your market)
Start decluttering: donate, sell, or discard
Gather key documents: deed, survey, HOA docs, warranties, permits, and receipts for improvements
Decide on your timeline and your next move (buy, rent, relocate) so closing dates line up
seller.tip: Pro tip: buyers see your home online first. The cleaning and repairs you do now show up in your listing photos.

seller.title: Get market ready
items: Complete necessary repairs and cosmetic touch-ups (fresh neutral paint goes a long way)
Deep clean the entire home: consider professional cleaning, including windows and carpets
Consider professional staging or a staging consultation
Boost curb appeal: landscaping, power wash, fresh mulch, paint or replace the front door
Begin packing non-essential and seasonal items
Rent a storage unit if needed to reduce clutter
Order a termite/WDO inspection: commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee
Check for open permits, liens, or unpaid HOA dues that could slow down closing

seller.title: Plan the launch
items: Schedule professional photography, video, and marketing materials
Set your listing price with your Realtor based on current market data
Complete your seller disclosures honestly and completely: Tennessee's residential property condition disclosure (or exemption), and lead-based paint disclosure for homes built before 1978
Establish your showing schedule and lockbox access
Create a home features sheet and maintenance binder for the buyer
Get quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies: book early for month-end dates

seller.title: Listing & offers
items: Keep the home show-ready at all times: beds made, counters clear, lights on
Secure valuables, medications, and important papers during showings
Have a plan for pets during showings
Review showing feedback with me regularly and adjust strategy if needed
Compare offers on more than price: financing type, earnest money, contingencies, appraisal terms, and closing date
Negotiate terms, repairs, and closing date with your Realtor's guidance
Accept an offer and go under contract

seller.title: Under contract
items: Confirm the earnest money has been delivered to the title company
Accommodate the buyer's home inspection and any re-inspections
Review repair requests with me and negotiate within the due diligence period
Provide appraiser access when requested
Request your HOA payoff or resale documents, if applicable
Begin packing in earnest: room by room, label everything
Confirm your closing date, time, and location
Schedule utility transfers for closing day. Keep services on through the buyer's final walkthrough.
Arrange final move-out cleaning (professional or DIY)
Pause lawn care, pest control, and other recurring services around closing

seller.title: Final week
items: Finish packing all remaining items
Confirm moving company or truck rental details in writing
Gather all keys, garage remotes, mailbox keys, and gate codes
Leave appliance manuals, warranties, and paint colors for the buyer
Complete any agreed repairs and keep the receipts to share
Remove everything that isn't staying with the home, and leave it broom-clean
Do a personal walkthrough: check every closet, attic, and garage
Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust if you're receiving proceeds by wire. Never rely on emailed instructions: wire fraud is real.
Review your settlement statement for accuracy and prepare a file of closing documents to bring

seller.title: Closing day
items: Bring a valid government-issued photo ID
Sign closing documents at the title company: ask about anything unclear
Hand over all keys and access devices
Confirm wire or check receipt for your proceeds
Take a final photo of your home: you earned this moment

seller.title: After the move
items: Update your address with USPS, banks, insurance providers, DMV, and your employer
File a change of address with the IRS (Form 8822) and update voter registration
Cancel your homeowner's insurance only after closing is confirmed: never before
Cancel any remaining home services at the old address
Watch for your escrow refund from your old mortgage servicer
Keep your settlement statement and improvement records: talk with a tax professional about capital gains and the home-sale exclusion
Leave a review for your Realtor: it truly means the world!
